title: Vaisheshika (atoms)
hook: Vaisheshika's list of what the world is made of ends with two items that aren't stuff at all: the self, and a mind that can only hold one thing at a time

segments.voice: Yesterday in Vaisheshika, six kinds of thing in one falling mango, and the habit of seeing the seams: the person, the mood, the action. Today closes a week.

You're on the phone, nodding along, and at the same time reading an email. Then the voice on the phone says, "So what do you think?" And there's a little gap. You heard every word. Or did you? The sound reached your ears. But something wasn't connecting. Vaisheshika had no phones, but it noticed that kind of gap, and used it as evidence: that gap, the school said, is how you know there's a mind. Today the school finishes its list of what the world is made of, and the last two items are you.
screen: `ON THE PHONE, READING EMAIL.` → `"SO WHAT DO YOU THINK?"` → `THE GAP IS EVIDENCE.`

segments.voice: Yesterday's first category was substance, and the Vaisheshika Sutra names nine. Earth, water, fire, air: the four kinds of atom. Then akasha, the space that carries sound. Then time and direction, which let us say before and after, here and there. And last, two that aren't stuff at all: the self, atman, and the mind, manas. Start with the self. How do you know there is one? The Sutra lists its marks, and the first is breathing out and breathing in. Then the eyelids opening and closing, life itself, the movement of the mind, and pleasure, pain, desire, aversion and effort. Breath is a sign of the self. Now the mind. Sometimes, the Sutra notes, self, senses and object are all in contact, and still no knowing happens. The phone talked; you didn't take it in. Something has to be the gate, and that gate is the mind. In this school the mind is tiny, so it can join only one sense at a time. On this view, nobody truly reads the email and hears the call at once; the mind only switches, quickly, back and forth. So the week closes. Nyaya brought five steps said out loud, three kinds of talk, reasons that only look like reasons, and doubt as a doorway. Vaisheshika brought dharma at the start, the atoms, the seams. And at the end of its list, a breathing self and a mind that can only hold one thing at a time.
screen: `NINE SUBSTANCES.` · `BREATH IS A SIGN OF THE SELF.` · `THE MIND: ONE THING AT A TIME.` · `A WEEK OF NYAYA AND VAISHESHIKA.` · then, large: `ONE GATE, ONE THING.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes or lower your gaze, and stay with one thing: the breath going out and coming in, the first of the self's marks in the Sutra's list. When a sound pulls you away, that's the gate swinging; no problem, swing it back to the breath. If you pray, you can let each breath be offered, one at a time.
Vaisheshika. Its nine substances end with the self, known by signs like breathing, and the mind, a gate that lets in one thing at a time.
Your line: Vaisheshika, atoms. The mind is one gate, for one thing at a time. A week of two schools, done.

howItsDone: Students of Vaisheshika learn the nine substances, from earth to mind, as part of the school's list of categories, and the Nyaya-Vaisheshika tradition uses the self's marks in its arguments that the self is real.

chat.meaning: The Sutra notes that self, senses and object can all be in contact and still no knowing happens. The mind, tiny, is the gate.

notes: Editor pass: removed lines telling the listener what they feel ('awful little gap', 'might surprise you') and the 'long before' time claim; the one-sense-at-a-time point is now framed as the school's view, not said to the listener as fact.
Week end (days 1163–1169): the look-back names Nyaya 1162–1165 (five members, three kinds of talk, hetvabhasa, doubt) and Vaisheshika 1166–1168.
Vaisheshika Sutra 1.1.5 lists nine dravyas (prthivi, ap, tejas, vayu, akasha, kala, dik, atman, manas): confirm the reference.

Marks of the self, Vaisheshika Sutra 3.2.4: prana/apana, nimesha/unmesha, life, movement of mind, affections of other senses, sukha, duhkha, iccha, dvesha, prayatna. Paraphrased; confirm the list and order ('the first is breathing out and breathing in').

Mark of mind, 3.2.1: knowledge arising or not despite contact of self, sense and object. The atomic size of manas and one-sense-at-a-time are standard Nyaya-Vaisheshika teaching (compare Nyaya Sutra 1.1.16 and 3.2.56ff); confirm phrasing 'tiny'.
Akasha described as 'the space that carries sound' (sound as its quality) and dik as 'direction': confirm the glosses.
